sensor.polarization: HH (co-pol, better water/land contrast than HV)

study_box.note: All areas are measured within this study box only.

clipping_note: KRS reservoir extends west to ~76.35°E but our NISAR frame starts at ~76.45°E. The western inflow tails (Hemavathi/Cauvery confluence) are outside the frame. Estimated coverage: ~55-65% of the full reservoir.

validation.confidence: MODERATE. Shoreline shape matches optical imagery. Areas are plausible for the visible portion of KRS. Cannot verify absolute accuracy without ground truth or coincident optical imagery for the same dates. Wind roughening may cause 2-4 dB omission error on windy days.

methodology.threshold_rationale: Calibrated -16.0 dB. Over KRS reservoir, open water HH backscatter ranges from -16.2 to -20 dB due to wind roughening and surface capillary waves, while surrounding land is brighter (-11.0 to -13.3 dB). -16.0 dB reliably preserves the contiguous reservoir body across both windy monsoon and calm post-monsoon conditions while preventing leakage into surrounding agricultural fields.
methodology.hh_vs_hv: HV median is ~-19 to -20 dB, too close to water threshold for reliable separation. HH has 8+ dB contrast between water (-20 to -25 dB) and land (-8 to -12 dB). HH is used.

green_patch_near_dam: The green (seasonal gain) patch near the dam (~76.57°E, 12.44°N, ~1.5 km north of dam wall along the eastern embayment) represents ~1.19 km² where backscatter shifted from -15.5 to -15.8 dB in Nov 2025 to -16.2 to -16.5 dB in Nov 2026. Physical & radar analysis: This reflects two coupled factors: (1) True seasonal shoreline advance and shallow water inundation along the eastern bay; and (2) Radar interaction with topography: steep rocky embankments and dam structures cause corner reflection / double-bounce artifacts that brighten nearshore water by 1-3 dB, placing marginal pixels right around the -16 dB threshold. We treat this as a known SAR boundary effect rather than a large physical flood event.
